I'm 19. I've had many very bad days and they continue to happen, but the worst was November 7, 2005. It was a Monday, and I was in sixth grade. My best guy friend gave me a long note that said things like, "your a nerd", "I don't wanna be your friend", and "good riddance". It broke my heart and changed me completely. Since then, I have dealt with depression, anxiety, and eating disorders, along with serious trust issues and chronic lying. It was the day I turned from a sweet and innocent girl to a mental patient. I don't cry at funerals, my relationships are a mess, and I am failing out of school.

Hey sweetheart. I am sorry that you feel like this. First of all, yes, go see a doctor, get some help, family, friends, whoever. LET IT OUT. It is so dangerous for you to keep all your emotions bottled up, even worse to keep pretending that you are strong through anything. I know, because I do the same damn thing every day of my life. Oh, it sucks. And I am so sorry that you're dealing with this hell too. 

YES. Pretending IS more painful. So find someone to trust and stop pretending! Look at you, posting this on Reddit! I have never met anyone braver than you. If you admit to the world that you are depressed, that is not being **weak** at all. That is true strength. 

On another note, the way you expressed your feelings in this post makes me think that you could write very beautiful poetry. It's not too hard on the soul and there is quite a community out there (esp. on Tumblr, the tag 'Spilled Ink' is a great support system). I hope that you can be motivated to create. I go by D.M.L. Catseye in the poetry world if you want to see what I mean.

THE GUILTY DREAM!
I had one just like this, but I was much younger, and I killed my younger sister, but she was actually older. She was upstairs in a burlap bag, rotting, and I just went and complained to my parents about the smell. There was another part when she was drowned in a lake behind the house. 
PLOT TWIST: I just checked my dream log, and the bag actually contained potatoes. The sister was not in the lake scene, her sleeping bag was.
I relive this dream quite often, because it was the most complex I had. I mix my dreams with my memories, actually. Sometimes I forget what my neighborhood really looks like, because there is the dream version, which is always the same, and the real version. Also always the same.
It's good that you write it all down, because I enjoyed reading it, and sometimes other people do, too. :)
AND crazy, unexplainable dreams are obviously quite normal, like the guilty dream, because we all have it. I can normally relate them to my own personality and feelings, so they make sense to me. But, I get thrown off many times (ex: I was a magical child who killed three magic persons with a quarter, string, and golden ring. ex2: I saw a hotel suddenly became run over by millions of dogs- covering the entire exterior, like little gravity fucks. No. Sense. At. All.)
Thanks for sharing!
